questionText: Let $A$ be any $n \times m$ matrix, where $m > n$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the system of linear equations $Ax = \mathbf{0}$ ?
options: There exist at least $m - n$ linearly independent solutions to this system
There exist $m - n$ linearly independent vectors such that every solution is a linear combination of these vectors
There exists a non-zero solution in which at least $m - n$ variables are 0
There exists a solution in which at least $n$ variables are non-zero
explanation:
Step 1: Understand Matrix Dimensions and Rank-Nullity Theorem
The given matrix $A$ has size $n \times m$ with $m > n$.
This corresponds to a homogeneous system of linear equations $Ax = \mathbf{0}$ with $n$ equations and $m$ variables.
The rank $r = \text{rank}(A)$ satisfies $r \le \min(n, m) = n$.

Step 2: Analyze Statement (A)
By the Rank-Nullity Theorem:
$\text{Nullity}(A) = m - r$
Since $r \le n$, we have $-r \ge -n$, which gives:
$\text{Nullity}(A) = m - r \ge m - n$
The nullity represents the dimension of the solution space (null space) of $Ax = \mathbf{0}$. A solution space of dimension at least $m - n$ contains at least $m - n$ linearly independent solution vectors.
Hence, Statement (A) is TRUE.

Step 3: Analyze Statement (B)
If $r < n$, then $\text{Nullity}(A) = m - r > m - n$. Any set of $m - n$ vectors can span a subspace of dimension at most $m - n$, which is insufficient to span the entire $(m - r)$-dimensional solution space.
Hence, Statement (B) is FALSE.

Step 4: Analyze Statement (C)
Consider the counterexample $A = [1 \ \ 1 \ \ 1]$ (a $1 \times 3$ matrix with $n = 1, m = 3$). Here $m - n = 2$.
If we set at least $m - n = 2$ variables to 0 (say $x_2 = 0, x_3 = 0$), then $Ax = 0 \implies x_1 + 0 + 0 = 0 \implies x_1 = 0$. The only solution is the zero vector $(0, 0, 0)^T$. So no non-zero solution exists in this case.
Hence, Statement (C) is FALSE.

Step 5: Analyze Statement (D)
Consider $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ (a $2 \times 3$ matrix with $n = 2, m = 3$).
The system $Ax = \mathbf{0}$ yields $x_1 = 0$ and $x_2 = 0$. Every solution is of the form $(0, 0, x_3)^T$, which has at most 1 non-zero variable, whereas $n = 2$. Thus, no solution exists with at least $n = 2$ non-zero variables.
Hence, Statement (D) is FALSE.
